title: Development and Internal Validation of the SpinePROTECT Score for Biopsychosocial Risk Stratification Before Elective Spine Surgery
summary:
Recovery after spine surgery is influenced not only by the underlying disorder and the surgical procedure. Psychological distress, the way patients cope with pain, the duration of symptoms, the use of strong pain medication, and previous operations may also affect recovery.
The aim of this study is to develop and evaluate the SpinePROTECT Score. The score is intended to combine physical, psychological, and surgery-related factors and may in the future help identify patients who have an increased risk of an unfavorable recovery.
The study will include 300 adults undergoing planned surgery for a degenerative disorder of the cervical, thoracic, or lumbar spine. Before surgery, participants will complete questionnaires, and clinical and surgery-related information will be collected. Further assessments will take place six weeks, three months, and twelve months after surgery.
Participation in the study will not change the treatment provided. The preliminary SpinePROTECT Score will not be used to decide whether surgery should be performed or to determine a particular treatment.
conditions: Degenerative disorders of the cervical, thoracic, and lumbar spine requiring elective surgical treatment

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Scheduled elective primary or revision surgery for a degenerative disorder of the cervical, thoracic, or lumbar spine.
2. Ability to understand the nature, purpose, and implications of the study and to provide written informed consent.
3. Sufficient German-language proficiency to complete the standardized questionnaires independently.
4. Willingness and expected ability to participate in follow-up assessments at 6 weeks, 3 months, and 12 months after surgery.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Emergency surgery.
2. Surgery for acute trauma, spinal infection, or spinal tumor disease.
3. Inability to provide informed consent.
4. Insufficient German-language proficiency to complete the study questionnaires.
5. Unwillingness or expected inability to participate in the scheduled postoperative follow-up assessments.
